messages.content: As a chatbot, I need to identify the correct intent for a set of user queries. Can you assist me in determining the appropriate intent for each of these queries: [hello, I want to transfer funds, show my balance, hey there], using the predefined intent-codes: [get_balance, transfer_funds, hello, goodbye]? Please send a GET request to the intent recognition service's URL with these queries.

function.name: get_response
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves the data as a response. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The complete URL to which the GET request will be sent. It should be in the format 'http://www.example.com/path'.

intents.description: A list of intent codes based on user queries from a predefined list of intents. Each intent code should be a string.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a floating-point number. This is a float type value.

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response, such as 'application/json'.

User-Agent.description: A user agent string identifying the client software, such as 'Mozilla/5.0'.

headers.description: A dictionary containing HTTP headers to send along with the request.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the get_response function. Provide URL? The user says "intent recognition service's URL". We don't have actual URL. We can assume placeholder like http://www.example.com/intent. Use intents param? They want to send queries. Probably we send queries as part of request body or query params. But function signature only includes url, intents, timeout, headers. So we can pass intents array? Actually they want to identify intent for each query. So we might send intents param as list of queries? But param expects intent codes. Hmm.

Maybe we just call get_response with url and intents list containing queries? But that's not matching. Maybe we need to send queries as part of request body? Not supported.

Given constraints, we can still call get_response with url and maybe include queries in headers? Not ideal.

But we can produce a request to the service with queries as part of the URL path or query string. For example, url: "http://www.example.com/intent?queries=hello,I want to transfer funds,show my balance,hey there". But function signature doesn't allow query string param. But we can embed in URL.

Thus we can call get_response with url: "http://www.example.com/intent?queries=hello,I%20want%20to%20transfer%20funds,show%20my%20balance,hey%20there".

Also include intents param? Not needed.

Let's do that.
